newsitem.title: USA: Natgas futures still down late with cash, charts.
newsitem.headline: Natgas futures still down late with cash, charts.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures were still down sharply late Thursday in moderately active trade, undermined by a softer cash and more technical selling after yesterday's reversal, industry sources said.
At 1430 EDT, November skidded 11.5 cents to $2.46 per million British thermal units, while December was 10.1 cents lower at $2.575. Most others were off by 1.5 to 10 cents.

"The screen (November) could move down into the $2.30s, but there should be some good buying there. There's still a lot of folks long though," said one Houston-based trader, noting mild weather forecasts were pressuring the cash.

Traders said 10-15 day forecasts for mostly seasonal to above-seasonal U.S. weather were likely to set a bearish tone during bidweek next week and keep the cash on the defensive for a while, particularly with eastern storage in good shape.
"The weather forecast has people concerned," said another trader, noting more talk of utility turn backs because of the mild weather.

Technically, traders said Wednesday's technical reversal and Thursday's follow through were likely to trigger more selling near-term. They said a December close below $2.60 could force prices into the mid-$2.40s or lower until colder weather finally kicks in.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices skidded almost a dime Thursday to about the $2.50 level. Midcon pipes were down a similar amount to the mid-$2.30s. Mild East Coast weather pressured New York city gate gas prices 15 cents lower to the low-$2.80 area.
NYMEX said 33,035 Hub contracts traded at 1300 EDT.
NYMEX November Hub futures expire Friday, October 25.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas edged up a penny to $1.115, while December was one-half cent higher at $1.15.
NYMEX November Alberta natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.
NYMEX Permian natgas was still untraded at 1430 EDT, but November was bid 13 cents lower at $2.25.
NYMEX November Permian natgas expires Tuesday, October 29.
On the KCBT, November fell two cents to $2.38, while most deferreds were down by one-half to 10 cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 9.5 cents to eight cents (NYMEX premium).
KCBT November natgas expires Monday, October 28.
